channel.title: Plain Earnings — new reports
channel.description: New earnings reports explained in plain English, with interactive money-flow charts.

item.title: Moderna — Q3 2026 earnings, explained
item.description: Moderna swung back to a profit on 29% revenue growth, but the profit is thin and the cost cuts did as much work as the sales rebound — and the fat cash balance came from a $3 billion convertible-note raise, not from operations.

item.title: Microsoft — FY27 Q1 earnings, explained
item.description: Microsoft grew 19% to $92.3B on Azure's 48% surge, and customers have now committed $677B of future cloud spending — the AI boom is real, and so is the bill to build it.

item.title: Alphabet — Q3 2026 earnings, explained
item.description: Google's operating profit rose 30% and Cloud more than doubled — but an $8.7B paper loss on its stock holdings turned the bottom line down 24%.

item.title: Amazon — Q3 2026 earnings, explained
item.description: Amazon's operating profit jumped 61% as AWS accelerated to 39% growth — but net income slipped, because last year's quarter included a $9.5B one-off Anthropic gain, and free cash flow went deeply negative on AI data-center spending.

item.title: Meta Platforms — Q3 2026 earnings, explained
item.description: Meta's ads grew 26% to $64.6B, but a $9.9B legal settlement cut operating profit by more than a third — and the number to watch is the $7.40 it would have earned without it.

item.title: Berkshire Hathaway — Q3 2026 earnings, explained
item.description: Berkshire's operating profit slipped 5.8% as GEICO's claims costs jumped, but the real story is the $9.6 billion buyback — more than the whole first half combined — while the 28% drop in headline profit mostly reflects smaller stock-market gains than last year, not weaker businesses.

item.title: Nvidia — Q2 FY27 earnings, explained
item.description: Nvidia's revenue more than doubled to $96.2B on the Blackwell Ultra ramp — data centers are now 93% of the business — but $7.8B of the $59.7B profit came from gains on its stock portfolio, not from selling chips.

item.title: Apple — Q4 FY26 earnings, explained
item.description: Apple's September quarter set records — $114.5B in revenue, iPhone up 17% to $57.6B — with Services at an all-time high and a one-off tariff refund adding a point to the margin.

item.title: Microsoft — Q4 FY26 earnings, explained
item.description: Microsoft closed fiscal 2026 with $90B in revenue, Azure up 43% and past $100B for the year — and a $3.2B Anthropic gain flattered the bottom line.

item.title: NVIDIA — Q1 FY26 earnings, explained
item.description: Nvidia's revenue jumped 69% to $44.1B on AI data-center demand, but a $4.5B charge for H20 chips blocked from China cut gross margin to 60.5% — without it, earnings would have been $0.96 a share instead of $0.76.

item.title: Apple — Q3 FY25 earnings, explained
item.description: Apple set a June-quarter revenue record — $94.0B, up 10% — with iPhone up 13% to $44.6B and Services at an all-time high of $27.4B.

item.title: Microsoft — FY25 Q3 earnings, explained
item.description: Microsoft grew 13% to $70.1B as Azure jumped 33% and the cloud passed $42B — AI demand is lifting every part of the business, even while the data-center buildout pushes costs up faster than revenue.

item.title: CoreWeave — Q1 2026 earnings, explained
item.description: CoreWeave's revenue more than doubled to $2.1B and its backlog reached $99.4B, but $536M of net interest turned a $144M operating loss into a $740M net loss.

item.title: Arm Holdings — Q1 FY27 earnings, explained
item.description: Arm's revenue hit a record $1.29B, up 22%, with data center royalties more than doubling — but GAAP profit stayed thin at $270M, and nearly half of it came from gains on investments, not the chip business.

item.title: Amazon — Q1 2024 earnings, explained
item.description: Amazon's sales rose 13% to $143.3B and operating income more than tripled to $15.3B as AWS reaccelerated to 17% growth and International turned profitable — and it kept $10.4B as profit even after a $2.0B paper loss on its Rivian stake.

item.title: Arm Holdings — Q4 FY26 earnings, explained
item.description: Arm closed fiscal 2026 with a record $1.49B quarter, up 20%, as licensing hit a record $819M — but GAAP profit of $313M was less than half the $641M non-GAAP figure, mostly because of $261M of share-based pay.

item.title: CoreWeave — Q4 2025 earnings, explained
item.description: CoreWeave's revenue more than doubled to $1.6B and its backlog reached $66.8B, but $388M of net interest turned an $89M operating loss into a $452M net loss.

item.title: NVIDIA — Q3 FY24 earnings, explained
item.description: Nvidia's revenue tripled to a record $18.1B as Data Center sales jumped 279% on AI demand — and it kept $9.2B as profit, about 51 cents of every dollar.

item.title: Apple — Q1 FY24 earnings, explained
item.description: Apple's sales grew 2% to $119.6B as Services set an all-time record and iPhone rose 6% — and EPS hit an all-time high of $2.18, with $33.9B kept as profit.

item.title: Alphabet — Q1 2024 earnings, explained
item.description: Alphabet grew revenue 15% to $80.5B as Search rose 14% and Google Cloud jumped 28% — and it kept $23.7B as profit, helped by a $2.2B paper gain on its investment stakes.

item.title: Hims & Hers — Q3 2026 earnings, explained
item.description: Revenue jumped 49% as international sales more than quadrupled, but Hims & Hers swung to a $33 million loss as gross margin collapsed 17 points and spending on marketing, admin and acquisitions piled up — growth bought at the cost of profitability.

item.title: Rocket Lab — Q3 2026 earnings, explained
item.description: Rocket Lab posted a record $268 million quarter with its backlog up 52% to $3.6 billion, but it still lost $80 million as Neutron development spending outran revenue — and the balance sheet now holds $4.4 billion in cash after a $3.9 billion share sale to fund the Iridium deal.

item.title: Datadog — Q4 2025 earnings, explained
item.description: Revenue grew 29% to $953 million and Datadog stayed profitable on a GAAP basis, but the GAAP operating margin was just 1% — stock-based pay is the wedge between the $9 million GAAP operating profit and $230 million non-GAAP.

item.title: Mastercard — Q4 2025 earnings, explained
item.description: Net revenue rose 18% to $8.8 billion as cross-border spending jumped 14% and value-added services grew 26% — and Mastercard kept $4.1 billion as profit, a 46% net margin.
